clauses.reason: The sole paragraph revokes Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940 (the abolition of Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee), the revocation of the Memphis, Chattanooga and Nashville port designations, and the extensions of District Nos. 42 and 45) and says the earlier order "is hereby revoked." It is a self-executing one-time act with no later effective date, condition or continuing duty, so it was performed and exhausted when the President signed it on February 8, 1940 (the signature block reads "February 8, 1940."; filed February 9, 1940; Federal Register issue of February 10, 1940). The effect of the revocation survives as an accrued consequence, but the command is spent. No later instrument in the held record revokes, amends or restates this order. This is an own-terms end by performance, not an inference from a later cleanup instrument.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8341 of February 8, 1940 (5 FR 643, Federal Register issue of February 10, 1940) is a one-paragraph order whose only operative act is to revoke Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940, which had abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee), revoked the designations of Memphis, Chattanooga and Nashville as customs ports of entry, and extended the limits of District No. 42 (Kentucky) and District No. 45 (St. Louis). The held text says the earlier order "is hereby revoked." The act has no deferred effective date, condition, report or continuing duty, so it was performed and exhausted when signed on February 8, 1940. No instrument held in the repository revokes, amends or extends Executive Order 8341, so no earlier or later end displaces that date. The working text is the official Federal Register page text (machine-extracted from the PDF, OCR), not an authenticated transcription; the page number and date were read from it.
